entities.summary:
The Syriac Orthodox Church is an Oriental Orthodox communion rooted in the Syriac-speaking Christianity of late antique Syria and Mesopotamia. Tracing its distinct hierarchy especially after sixth-century miaphysite controversies, it preserved West Syriac liturgy, theology, and literary culture under Byzantine, Islamic, and later Ottoman rule.

Headquartered in later centuries at Damascus’s Cathedral of Saint George, the church ministered to communities across the Middle East and, after modern diasporas, to parishes worldwide. Monasteries and scholars transmitted Syriac as a sacred and scholarly language even as political borders shifted.

The Syriac Orthodox tradition stands among the oldest continuous Christian institutions, embodying how Oriental Orthodoxy survived empire, persecution, and migration without Latin or Byzantine conformity.
